events.title: Cicero is born
events.description: Marcus Tullius Cicero, the future Roman orator, lawyer and statesman, was born in Arpinum, southeast of Rome. He rose to become consul of the Roman Republic.
events.significance: His speeches, letters and philosophical writings shaped Latin prose and later European political thought. They are also a major source for the final years of the Roman Republic.

events.title: Martin Luther is excommunicated
events.description: Pope Leo X issued the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem. It formally expelled the German monk Martin Luther from the Catholic Church after he refused to retract his criticisms of church practices.
events.significance: The excommunication made the break between Luther and Rome permanent. It pushed the Protestant Reformation toward a lasting split in Western Christianity.

events.title: Washington wins the Battle of Princeton
events.description: After his surprise victory at Trenton, George Washington slipped away from a larger British force. He then defeated a detachment of British troops near Princeton, New Jersey.
events.significance: Together with Trenton, the victory revived American morale at a low point in the Revolutionary War. It also helped keep the Continental Army in the field through the winter.

events.title: J.R.R. Tolkien is born
events.description: John Ronald Reuel Tolkien was born in Bloemfontein, in what is now South Africa. He later became an Oxford professor of language and literature.
events.significance: Tolkien wrote The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. His books established modern epic fantasy and remain among the best-selling and most influential works of the 20th century.

events.title: Alaska becomes the 49th U.S. state
events.description: President Dwight D. Eisenhower proclaimed Alaska's admission to the Union. It became the largest state by area and the first new state added since 1912.
events.significance: Statehood gave Alaska's residents full representation in Congress. It also brought the country's northernmost territory into a stronger role in national affairs, including resource development and defense.
